profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a children's hospital between the pediatric residency research team and the clinical informatics implementation lead. The team is preparing a small live-unit rollout that adapts findings from a pilot study on patient photographs during handoffs into the evening sign-out workflow on the general pediatrics floor. The immediate agenda is to align on what materials will be ready for next Monday's nurse-physician handoff simulation, what version of the patient-photo handoff packet will be used, how consented photographs will move from the EHR into the handoff tool, and who is responsible for the final training and privacy checklist. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on the handoff packet, the training deliverable, the go-live readiness status, and the ownership of the shared implementation documents.

members.name: Dr. Maya Chen
members.role: Pediatric Hospitalist and Study Operations Lead
members.expertise: Resident handoff workflow, simulation-based study operations, inpatient pediatric communication
members.background: Dr. Chen is a hospitalist who helped run the original pilot sessions with pediatric residents and now coordinates the clinical side of a limited implementation on one pediatric unit.
members.private_state: She wants the rollout to feel lightweight and clinically acceptable so unit staff will not resist it, and she is especially worried that delays over documentation details will jeopardize the Monday simulation.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the 'handoff packet,' they mean the resident-facing sign-out printout used during evening verbal sign-out, not the broader training and privacy materials.
The 'latest photo list' refers to the set of patient images already manually verified by the study coordinator from the last consent sweep on Thursday afternoon.
A unit being 'ready' means the workflow has been rehearsed and the visible handoff materials are usable, even if some audit logging and edge-case documentation are still being finalized.
If someone says informatics will 'upload the photos,' that means placing the approved image thumbnails into the sign-out view from the coordinator's export, not building a fully automated EHR feed.
The shared implementation checklist is operationally owned by the clinical team unless informatics explicitly asks to revise a technical section.

members.name: Alex Romero
members.expertise: EHR workflow configuration, HIPAA-compliant media handling, cross-team implementation coordination
members.background: Alex manages inpatient informatics rollouts and has been asked to support the photo-enabled handoff workflow by coordinating EHR extracts, access controls, and implementation artifacts.
members.private_state: He wants to keep the rollout compliant and reproducible so it does not create an exception process that later becomes hard to govern, and he is concerned that the clinical team underestimates dependencies around photo provenance and documentation.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the 'handoff packet,' they mean the full implementation bundle for the pilot day: sign-out view, tip sheet, privacy language, and the downgrade plan if a photo is unavailable.
The 'latest photo list' means the most recent EHR media extract generated overnight from currently flagged consented patients, because a manually checked list can become stale by the next shift.
A unit being 'ready' means all required artifacts, audit steps, and fallback instructions are complete enough that support staff could run the workflow without improvised clarification.
If the team agrees informatics will 'upload the photos,' that implies using the approved secure import path tied to the media repository and patient identifiers, not a coordinator-managed file drop.
The shared implementation checklist stays under informatics document control once it contains privacy and systems steps, even if clinicians contribute content.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the handoff packet
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to 'finalize the handoff packet by Friday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the resident-facing sign-out printout with patient names, one-line summaries, and the approved photo thumbnail layout for the simulation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the entire rollout bundle: sign-out printout, quick-reference training sheet, privacy reminder text, exception workflow, and support contact line.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In a coordination meeting, 'packet' sounds like an ordinary shared artifact, and both participants regularly use bundled materials; each hears the phrase as naturally referring to their own workstream's default scope.

misalignment_points.topic: Which photo list is the latest one
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to using the 'latest photo list' for Monday's simulation.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the Thursday manually verified spreadsheet of consented children prepared by the study coordinator after bedside confirmation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the automated overnight Saturday/Sunday EHR media extract of active admitted patients with photo consent flags.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both lists are real, current, and plausibly authoritative, and 'latest' feels self-explanatory; neither expects that the other team's default source of recency differs.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the unit should be 'ready' by Monday afternoon.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes readiness means residents can perform the simulated sign-out with visible photographs and a brief verbal reminder about privacy.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes readiness means the workflow can run end-to-end under standard support conditions, including documented fallback steps, access validation, and logging checks.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Readiness is a common project-status term that usually compresses many details; because both are trying to be efficient and optimistic, they accept the shared label without unpacking the threshold.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that informatics will 'upload the photos before the session.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects Alex's team to take the coordinator's approved image file set and place thumbnails into the existing handoff view as a one-time prep step for the simulation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects his team to run the standard secure import workflow from the hospital media repository, requiring properly matched identifiers and the current consented-patient extract.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The task sounds operationally straightforward and not like a strategic choice, so neither side treats the method as something needing explicit discussion; each assumes there is only one obvious compliant way to do it.

turns.inner_thought: I need this meeting to stay practical. For Monday, what matters is that the residents can rehearse evening sign-out on the peds floor with the photo thumbnails visible on the resident-facing sign-out printout. If we can finalize that handoff packet by Friday, we can still run the simulation even if some of the backend documentation pieces are still being polished. To me, the unit is ready once the workflow has been walked through and the visible materials work at the bedside and during sign-out.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making time. I want to keep us focused on getting the pediatrics floor ready for Monday's photo-enabled handoff simulation. If we can finalize the handoff packet by Friday, I think we're in good shape.

turns.inner_thought: That timeline is workable if we mean the full implementation bundle and not just the printout. I need the handoff packet to include the quick guidance, privacy reminder language, fallback plan, and support contact details so staff aren't improvising. I also need to confirm we're using the latest photo list from the overnight extract, because a manually verified list from earlier in the week may already be out of date by Monday.
turns.utterance: That should work from my side. I mainly want to confirm we're all using the latest photo list for Monday, and make sure the handoff packet includes what staff will need on the day.

turns.inner_thought: Good, he's aligned. The coordinator already cleaned up the Thursday spreadsheet after bedside consent review, so that latest photo list is the one we've been treating as final. Residents really do not need a giant bundle; they need the sign-out pages and maybe a brief privacy reminder at the start so this feels lightweight and doesn't trigger pushback. I don't want this to expand into extra materials that slow us down before Monday.
turns.utterance: Yes, the coordinator already cleaned up the latest photo list after the bedside consent review, so we have a solid version to work from. From the resident side, they mainly need the sign-out pages and a short reminder.

turns.inner_thought: Okay, if they have a reference list that's fine, but my team still needs to use the current extract as the authoritative source before we move anything. When I say we'll upload the photos before the session, I mean we'll run the approved secure import workflow against the current consented-patient extract and connect those images into the handoff view in the standard way. That keeps provenance and identifiers defensible.
turns.utterance: Great. Informatics can upload the photos before the session once my team runs the current extract and ties it into the handoff view.

turns.inner_thought: Perfect, that's exactly what I needed to hear: he'll take the coordinator's approved image set and place the thumbnails into the sign-out view. I'll just have her send the manually verified image file set over so his team can plug those in. If we keep it as a one-time prep step for the simulation, we can avoid turning this into a larger operational fight.
turns.utterance: Sounds great. I'll have the coordinator send over the approved image set so your team can upload the photos before the session, and we can keep the workflow lightweight.

turns.inner_thought: I still need a few things in place before I'd call this ready. If the packet has fallback instructions for when a photo isn't available and the privacy language is included, then support staff can handle exceptions without ad hoc explanations. Readiness to me means the workflow can run end-to-end under normal conditions, not just during a guided rehearsal.
turns.utterance: One other piece: if we add the fallback instructions and the privacy language to the handoff packet, then the unit should be ready by Monday afternoon.

turns.inner_thought: That's reasonable enough. For me, once residents have rehearsed with the patient-photo sign-out pages and we've reminded them how to handle the conversation, we're ready. I hear his add-ons as minor supporting details, not gating items. I really need to avoid another round of delay over edge-case paperwork.
turns.utterance: I agree, the unit should be ready by Monday afternoon. Once the residents rehearse with the patient-photo sign-out pages, I think the workflow will be set for the simulation.

turns.inner_thought: I'll keep control of the implementation checklist since it now includes privacy and systems steps. I need to document access validation and the import steps there so the packet is complete and reproducible. If this becomes a standing workflow later, we'll need a clean audit trail of how it was configured and supported.
turns.utterance: That makes sense. I'll keep the implementation checklist updated with access validation and the import steps so the handoff packet is complete.

Operationally, the checklist lives with the clinical team unless informatics specifically needs to revise a section, and I don't want version-control churn to bog this down. As long as the sign-out printout is finalized, we can move.
turns.utterance: Perfect. I'll make the final edits to the handoff packet Friday morning, and I assume you can append anything technical after that.
